meta.title: Which brain cells change in dementia?

meta.regionPlain: a part of the brain behind the temple, involved in memory and language

measure.label: How common this cell type is

caveats: This measures RNA, not protein. A gene being switched on does not prove it is doing something.
These are brains studied after death. They show one moment, not the change over time.

cellScreen.averageSentence: On average, {{meanDementia}} in {{groupDementiaShort}}, compared with {{meanNormal}} in {{groupNormalShort}}.

verdict.up: That is a {{effectSize}} difference: {{direction}} in {{groupDementiaShort}}. Higher means {{higherMeans}}.
verdict.down: That is a {{effectSize}} difference: {{direction}} in {{groupDementiaShort}}. Higher means {{higherMeans}}.
verdict.none: The two groups are about the same.

cellScreen.stableNote: This one barely changes — and a row that stays flat is a result too.
cellScreen.figCaptionDonors: {{measureLabel}} — {{unit}}. Each small dot is one person; the big dots are the averages.
cellScreen.gapPrompt: Ask yourself: is the gap between the two big dots bigger than the scatter of the small ones? If it is, the difference is more likely to be real.

cohensD.note: How many “spreads” apart the two averages are. This is the number to trust first.

pValue.note: Roughly how often a gap at least this big would turn up by chance if there were really no difference. It does not tell you the difference is important.

stats.whyPeople: Why people, not cells? This study measured {{cellsTotal}}, but they came from {{donorTotal}}. Cells from one person are alike, so counting every cell as separate evidence would make almost any difference look certain. The honest sample size is the number of people.
stats.genesChanged: Genes whose activity changed in this cell type: {{genesChanged}}.

geneMeasure.label: Average activity level of the gene

ratioWords.text: about one and a half times as much

geneScreen.figCaption: {{geneMeasureLabel}} in {{cellLabelLower}}, in {{geneUnit}}. The big dots are the averages; the bars show the spread between people.
geneScreen.verdict: In {{groupDementiaShort}} these cells make {{geneChange}} of this gene’s message.
geneScreen.verdictSame: In {{groupDementiaShort}} these cells make about the same amount of this gene’s message.

log2FC.note: One step up means double; one step down means half.

pValue.note: Never the headline: read the size of the change first.

geneScreen.elsewhereHeading: Where else is this gene switched on?
geneScreen.elsewhereCaption: The same gene in other cell types. Every cell carries the same DNA, but each type uses a different set of genes.
geneScreen.elsewhereNote: {{geneMeasureLabel}}, in {{geneUnit}}. Bars start at zero. The bar for this cell type uses {{groupNormalShort}}.
